summary: AI coding context files are project-level instruction files that coding assistants automatically load before helping, giving them persistent knowledge of your tech stack, conventions, architecture, and constraints without repeating it in every prompt. Each major tool reads a different file in a different location and format, so teams using multiple assistants often maintain several files (or symlink them). The highest-impact content is non-obvious project knowledge—build commands, architectural decisions, and rejected alternatives—rather than anything already evident from the code itself.

tools.name: CLAUDE.md
tools.purpose: Automatically loaded at the start of every session as persistent context: tech stack, build/test commands, coding standards, architectural decisions, and a map of the codebase structure. Supports progressive disclosure, referencing deeper docs by path so Claude loads them only when needed.
tools.limits: No hard documented character cap, but it counts against the context window on every session—keep it concise. Use the # key to append repeated instructions and /init to generate a starter file.
tips: Give Claude a 'map' of the codebase structure so it maintains context without manual reinforcement
Use progressive disclosure: keep the root file short and link to path/to/docs.md for complex topics
Use the # key during sessions to add instructions you find yourself repeating; they accumulate into CLAUDE.md
Run /init to bootstrap a CLAUDE.md that reflects your project
Place subdirectory CLAUDE.md files in monorepos for package-specific rules
Keep context fresh—prune stale instructions over time

tools.name: Cursor Rules
tools.purpose: Provides system-level instructions to Cursor's AI for code generation and chat. Modern .cursor/rules supports multiple scoped MDC files with metadata (always-apply, auto-attach by glob, agent-requested, or manual) so rules apply only to relevant files or contexts.
tools.limits: No official hard limit; rules should be focused and modular. The older single .cursorrules file is deprecated in favor of the .cursor/rules directory.
tips: Prefer the .cursor/rules directory with scoped MDC files over the legacy .cursorrules
Use glob patterns to auto-attach rules only to relevant files (e.g. *.tsx)
Keep each rule file focused on a single concern
Set 'always apply' only for truly global conventions to avoid bloating context

tools.name: Copilot Instructions
tools.purpose: Repository-wide custom instructions automatically added to Copilot Chat and agent requests, describing coding standards, frameworks, and project conventions so generated code matches the team's style.
tools.limits: No published character limit; GitHub recommends short, self-contained statements. Path-specific instruction files can be scoped with applyTo glob frontmatter.
tips: Keep instructions short, concrete, and in natural language
Avoid references to external resources Copilot can't access
Use .github/instructions/*.instructions.md with applyTo globs for path-specific rules
Don't include conflicting or vague directives like 'write good code'

tools.name: Windsurf Rules
tools.file_path: .windsurf/rules/*.md (directory, current) and .windsurfrules (legacy, project root); plus global rules
tools.purpose: Guides the Cascade agent with project conventions and constraints. Supports activation modes (always-on, manual, model-decision, glob-based) so rules apply contextually.
tools.limits: Windsurf documents a character budget: roughly 6,000 characters per rules file and a combined global+workspace cap (around 12,000 characters total); content beyond the limit is truncated.
tips: Stay within the per-file character budget or rules get truncated
Use activation modes to apply rules only when relevant
Split rules into multiple files under .windsurf/rules for organization
Write simple, specific bullet points rather than long prose

tools.name: Aider Conventions
tools.file_path: CONVENTIONS.md (added via --read or config) and .aider.conf.yml (project root or home dir)
tools.purpose: CONVENTIONS.md holds coding guidelines that Aider loads as read-only context so it follows your style; .aider.conf.yml configures model, auto-commits, read files, and other defaults so the conventions file is always included.
tools.limits: No hard limit, but since it's sent with requests, keep it concise to conserve tokens. Add it as read-only to avoid it being edited.
tips: Reference CONVENTIONS.md via the 'read' key in .aider.conf.yml so it loads automatically
Mark the conventions file read-only so Aider doesn't modify it
Keep conventions short—they're sent with every request and cost tokens
Use .aider.conf.yml to pin model and workflow defaults alongside conventions

tools.name: AGENTS.md
tools.tool: OpenAI Codex, and other agents (cross-tool standard)
tools.purpose: An open, tool-agnostic standard for agent instructions—setup commands, test instructions, conventions, and PR guidelines—adopted by multiple agents as a shared alternative to tool-specific files. Nearest AGENTS.md to an edited file takes precedence.
tools.limits: No defined limit; it's plain Markdown read into context, so keep it focused.
tips: Use AGENTS.md as a single cross-tool file when supporting multiple agents
Place nested AGENTS.md files for monorepo subprojects—closest one wins
Include concrete setup, build, and test commands
Some teams symlink CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md to avoid duplication

best_practices.title: Plan before implementation
best_practices.description: The highest-impact practice is encouraging planning before coding—via plan mode or annotation cycles. Context files that establish a 'research and plan first' expectation shape better implementation approaches across every task.

best_practices.title: Give the assistant a map of the codebase
best_practices.description: Describe the project's directory structure, key modules, and where things live so the tool maintains consistent context about your codebase without you re-explaining it each session.

best_practices.title: Document non-obvious constraints and decisions
best_practices.description: Capture architectural decisions, why certain patterns are required, and rejected alternatives with reasons (e.g. 'Never use raw SQL, prefer the ORM'). This is knowledge the model cannot infer from the code alone.

best_practices.title: Include concrete build, test, and run commands
best_practices.description: Spell out exact commands (e.g. 'Test with: pytest -x --tb=short') so the assistant runs the right tooling instead of guessing, reducing failed or inconsistent runs.

best_practices.title: Use progressive disclosure
best_practices.description: Keep the root file short and link to deeper documentation by path, so detailed references load only when the task needs them rather than bloating every session's context window.

best_practices.title: Specify conventions the tool should follow
best_practices.description: State formatting, naming, type-hint, and testing conventions explicitly (e.g. 'Always use type hints for function signatures') so generated code matches your team's style on the first pass.

best_practices.title: Grow the file organically and keep it fresh
best_practices.description: Add instructions you catch yourself repeating (Claude's # key) and prune stale guidance over time, so the file genuinely reflects how the team currently works.

best_practices.title: Scope rules in monorepos
best_practices.description: Use subdirectory/nested files or glob-based activation so package-specific rules only apply where relevant, avoiding one giant file with conflicting instructions.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting task tracking, TODOs, or project management notes in the context file
common_mistakes.fix: Keep the file about durable conventions and architecture; track tasks in an issue tracker or separate planning docs, not in the context file loaded every session.

common_mistakes.mistake: Documenting things that are already obvious from the code
common_mistakes.fix: Omit descriptions the model can read directly from source; reserve the file for non-obvious constraints, decisions, and commands it can't infer.

common_mistakes.mistake: Dumping debugging notes or git history into the file
common_mistakes.fix: Leave transient debugging context and history in commits, PRs, and comments; the context file should hold stable guidance only.

common_mistakes.mistake: Letting the file grow huge and unfocused
common_mistakes.fix: Use progressive disclosure and scoped files, stay within documented character budgets (e.g. Windsurf's ~6k/file), and prune regularly so it doesn't consume the context window.

common_mistakes.mistake: Writing vague directives like 'write clean code'
common_mistakes.fix: Replace them with specific, testable rules (exact commands, concrete naming/formatting conventions, explicit do/don't patterns).
Consolidate and scope rules with glob/activation modes so only relevant, non-conflicting guidance applies to a given file or task.

common_mistakes.mistake: Referencing external resources the tool can't access
common_mistakes.fix: Inline the necessary information or link to in-repo docs by path rather than pointing to external URLs the assistant cannot fetch.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using the deprecated single-file format when a directory format exists
common_mistakes.fix: Migrate from legacy .cursorrules/.windsurfrules to the modern .cursor/rules and .windsurf/rules directories for scoped, maintainable rules.
